description:
Resource/file fixtures abort at native struct field access with a kind mismatch:
- resource_lifecycle (run): runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1642 'fz_struct_get_named_field_ref: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(3), found: ValueKind(7) }' — a named-field read expects one kind (3) but the value is another (7).
- file_resource_lifecycle, a-resource_aot_dtor (build): resource destructor / AOT dtor legs fail.
- file_handle: fails its matrix leg (golden/output mismatch — confirm vs this struct-field issue).

Reconcile the struct schema/field-kind the resource lifecycle path lowers against the runtime value it produces, so named-field reads see the expected kind. Sits under the fz-go4 ownership-boundary work since resource handles cross the native boundary.

comments.text: SPIKE 2026-07-09: prototype 333085854 on branch coord/spike-fz-9i4-7-5-resource is promotable. Current HEAD reproduces only resource_lifecycle as the native panic; file_resource_lifecycle, a-resource_aot_dtor, and file_handle no longer share this failure. Root cause:  lowers as generic FieldAccess, backend/native preserve it as struct-field access, and native calls fz_struct_get_named_field_ref; resource handles are ValueKind::RESOURCE, so the struct read rejects them as ExpectedTag { expected: STRUCT, found: RESOURCE }. Prototype adds narrow resource.value handling to fz_struct_get_named_field_ref and backend interpreter interp_struct_field; resource_lifecycle passes run/interp/build. Promotion should pin resource.value through production paths, remove/adjust resource_lifecycle defers, and consider the semantic cleanup that R.unwrap/1[resource(a0_p)] still types as any instead of the payload type.

CORRECTION 2026-07-09: previous spike comment omitted the literal receiver syntax due shell quoting. The root-cause sentence should read: h.value lowers as generic FieldAccess, backend/native preserve it as struct-field access, and native calls fz_struct_get_named_field_ref.

title: [BUG] Resource-lifecycle native struct field access kind mismatch
